Radius of \(8^{\text {th }}\) orbit is four times larger than that of \(4^{\text {th }}\) orbit.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
\(\mathrm{r} \propto \mathrm{n}^2\)

questions.q: Maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in shell with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> are:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The maximum number of electrons that could be present in a shell is given by the rule 2n2.

Where n is the shell number.

The first shell K shell can accommodate a maximum of 2 electrons (2 × 12 = 2).

The second shell L shell can accommodate a maximum of 8 electrons (2 × 22 = 8).

Likewise, the 4th shell named N can accommodate a maximum of 32 electrons (2 × 42 = 2 × 16 = 32).

questions.q:
Which of the following pair is not isoelectronic species?
(Atomic numbers Sm=62; Er=68; Yb=70; Lu=71; Eu=63; Tb=65; Tm=69)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Isoelectronic species are those which have the same number of electrons.

The number of electrons in an ion is given by the atomic number minus the charge of the ion.

For $Sm^{2+}$, the number of electrons is $62 - 2 = 60$. For $Eu^{3+}$, the number of electrons is $63 - 3 = 60$. These are isoelectronic.

For $Yb^{2+}$, the number of electrons is $70 - 2 = 68$. For $Lu^{3+}$, the number of electrons is $71 - 3 = 68$. These are isoelectronic.

For $Eu^{2+}$, the number of electrons is $63 - 2 = 61$. For $Tb^{4+}$, the number of electrons is $65 - 4 = 61$. These are isoelectronic.

For $Tb^{2+}$, the number of electrons is $65 - 2 = 63$. For $Tm^{4+}$, the number of electrons is $69 - 4 = 65$. Since they have a different number of electrons, they are not isoelectronic. !

questions.q: The energy of an electron in the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom is -2.18×10-18 J Its energy in the third Bohr orbit is_______.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The energy of an electron in the $n$-th Bohr orbit of a hydrogen atom is given by the expression:

$E_n = \dfrac{E_1}{n^2}$

where $E_1$ is the energy of the electron in the first Bohr orbit.

Given $E_1 = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \text{ J}$.

For the third Bohr orbit, $n = 3$.

Substituting the value of $n$ into the expression for $E_n$:

$E_3 = \dfrac{E_1}{3^2}$

$E_3 = \dfrac{1}{9} E_1$

Therefore, the energy of the electron in the third Bohr orbit is $\dfrac{1}{9}\text{th}$ of its energy in the first Bohr orbit. ~

questions.q:
Heat treatment of muscular pain involves radiation of wavelength of about 900 nm . Which spectral line of H atom is suitable for this?
Given : Rydberg constant $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}=10^5 \mathrm{~cm}^{-1}, \mathrm{~h}=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~s}, \mathrm{c}=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ )
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \lambda=900 \mathrm{~nm} \quad \text { H-atom }(\mathrm{Z}=1) \\
& =9 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~cm} \\
& \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}=10^5 \mathrm{~cm}^{-1} \\
& \text { Ryderg eq. }=\frac{1}{\lambda}=\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} \mathrm{Z}^2 \times\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\lambda \times \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{9 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~cm} \times 10^5 \mathrm{~cm}^{-1}}=\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2}=\frac{1}{9}
\end{aligned}$

It is possible when $\mathrm{n}_1=3, \mathrm{n}_2=\infty$
Possible series : $\infty \rightarrow 3$
